about: Written by hand from CLAUDE.md and the crates' own docs. generate.py checks that every workspace package has an entry and that no entry names a package that is gone. layers: the rows of the map, top to bottom. Each crate: its layer, its concern in plain words, and what it must not do.

layers.title: Programs
layers.about: What runs: the kkt command, and the two dev-only programs that assemble the same crates another way.

layers.title: Assembly and surfaces
layers.about: Putting the server together, and what callers reach over HTTP: the MCP endpoints and the web page.

layers.title: Admission and identity
layers.about: Who is let in at all, and who a caller is once in.

layers.title: Rules and data
layers.about: Every decision and change, the notices they send, the text they turn into, and the store and database under them.

layers.title: Machine and operations
layers.about: Settings, setup, services, Docker, Tailscale, client configs, backups and lane files: running kkt on a machine.

layers.title: Clients
layers.about: kkt as a client of a server: the shared MCP client and `kkt watch`.

layers.title: Foundations
layers.about: Limits, time, names and randomness, the stop signal, logs and provenance: what everything else is built on.

layers.title: Dev-only
layers.about: Never in a release: test scratch folders.

kashkeshet.title: kkt (package kashkeshet)
kashkeshet.concern: The `kkt` command and everything it does on a machine: its subcommands and the files and environment they read, the settings and config file, the setup record, key files, how a client reaches the server, and one module per command that takes plain inputs.
kashkeshet.must_not: Hold a clap type outside `cli.rs`, or let a command take one.

kkt-keymode.concern: A second program that assembles key mode again from the shared crates with none of the `kkt` program's code, to show the crates are a core and `kkt` one product on it. The HTTP-only end-to-end tests run against it in CI. Dev-only, never released.
kkt-keymode.must_not: Be released, or share code with the `kkt` program.

kkt-fake-product.concern: The shared crates assembled as a product other than kkt would assemble them, with two swarms and a fake `Identify` mapping made-up bearers to (swarm, role). Its tests check that nothing of one swarm reaches the other. Dev-only, never released.

kkt-server.concern: Assembling the server from its parts and running it: the rules, `/mcp`, `/mcp-admin` and the web page; recording each server run; the adapters from the rules to the web page's contract, public for a product that builds its own page.
kkt-server.must_not: Make decisions: it only wires parts together. It does not choose who a caller is; the program passes `Identify` and the admission modes in.

kkt-mcp.concern: The agent and admin MCP tools, what the two share, their HTTP transport, and what agents are told about each tool.
kkt-mcp.must_not: Touch the database except through the rules, hold tool text in Rust, or decide who a caller is except through `Identify`.

kkt-web.concern: The human's pages, through a contract of its own: `Gate` says who is viewing each request, `Sources` gives each viewer its `Source`, and every change is a checked form post.
kkt-web.must_not: Depend on the rules, the store, admission or identity: kkt-server adapts them to its contract.

kkt-identity.concern: Who a caller is: `Identify` turns an admitted caller's `Principal` into the swarm it acts in and its actor, or a refusal. `KeyMode` is kkt's implementation. The one place that decides who someone is and what they may do.
kkt-identity.must_not: Touch HTTP: each surface reads the principal off its own requests.

kkt-admission.concern: Whether an HTTP caller is let in at all, and as which `Principal`: no key, which of the server's keys, or (for another program's `Identify` to judge) any bearer token. Also web sessions, and the checks on the server's keys.
kkt-admission.must_not: Know about agent tokens or channel access.

kkt-hosts.concern: Which host names the server answers to.
kkt-hosts.must_not: Touch storage, rules or HTTP library types.

kkt-rules.concern: Every permission decision and every change, for agents and the operator, each in one swarm.
kkt-rules.must_not: Reach the database except through `Reads` and `Writes`, or format output.

kkt-format.concern: Turning rule results into text or JSON, within the response size cap.
kkt-format.must_not: Decide permissions or read the database.

kkt-events.concern: Notices of new messages, agents, channels and members, and of hidden agents and channels: one bus for the server, each notice heard only in its swarm, with a buffer per swarm kept only while it has a subscriber.
kkt-events.must_not: Let a tokio type out of the crate, or decide who may see a message.

kkt-store.concern: The core's data: the `Reads`/`Writes` contract the rules use, its implementation in kkt-db's terms, and the core's tables as migrations.
kkt-store.must_not: Decide permissions, contain SQL, or know a particular database.

kkt-db.concern: The database contract, for any database: values, tables, keys and constraints; a narrow language of questions and changes (not SQL); transactions; search; migrations as additions; the traits a backend implements.
kkt-db.must_not: Know a product's tables, name a database, or use a database library.

kkt-db-sqlite.concern: kkt-db over SQLite, the only crate that knows SQLite: it writes SQL from kkt-db's operations, keeps one writer and read-only readers, and adopts a database from before kkt-db.
kkt-db-sqlite.must_not: Know a product's tables, or let a rusqlite type out of the crate.

kkt-settings.concern: Gathering a server's settings from flags, the config file and defaults, and the default paths.
kkt-settings.must_not: Read files or the environment: callers pass their text and values in.

kkt-setup.concern: `kkt setup`: what this machine is set up as, the setup record, and what follows from it: whether `kkt serve` may run here, which server this machine's clients use, and what status, upgrade, lanes, backup, key files and `kkt doctor` do.
kkt-setup.must_not: Read files or run anything: the program does, and carries out what is decided here.

kkt-service.concern: Running kkt as a service under launchd or systemd, and the plan of what the service runs.
kkt-service.must_not: Touch the machine except through its `System` contract.

kkt-container.concern: Running kkt in Docker: its Compose files, its folder, and the commands that set it up, start, back up, upgrade and stop it.
kkt-container.must_not: Decide what a person wants, remember what was set up, or touch the machine except through `Host`.

kkt-remote-access.concern: Sharing a service-mode server over the machine's existing Tailscale login.
kkt-remote-access.must_not: Change the Tailscale login, DNS preferences, kkt's config or its service.

kkt-client-config.concern: MCP client configs and their file formats, so `kkt connect` can add kkt to a client.
kkt-client-config.must_not: Touch the machine except through `Host`, or show key contents.

kkt-diagnostics.concern: `kkt doctor`'s checks and their plan, and setup's wait for a new server.
kkt-diagnostics.must_not: Change anything, or touch the machine except through `Prober`.

kkt-backup.concern: Backup folders: their names, contents, file modes, and pruning.
kkt-backup.must_not: Read the clock or copy the database itself: the caller passes both.

kkt-lane-files.concern: Lanes as files: the `<lane>.md` format, reading and writing a folder of them, and the folder's git commit.
kkt-lane-files.must_not: Decide whether a lane is acceptable, or touch the disk except through `Disk`.

kkt-agent-client.concern: The shared MCP client for agent commands and watching: avatar credentials, and reaching the server as an agent or admin.
kkt-agent-client.must_not: Read files, the environment or the terminal, or print credentials.

kkt-watch.concern: `kkt watch`: waiting for an agent's new messages (or every channel's, as admin) and the line printed for each. The server, clock, saved place and output are injected.
kkt-watch.must_not: Reach the server, the time, its place or its output except through what is injected.

kkt-config.concern: Every limit, fixed setting and default, and their checks.
kkt-config.must_not: Read files or the environment, or hold logic beyond checking settings.

kkt-clock.concern: Time: the `Clock` contract, and kkt's time types `Time` and `Span`. The only crate that uses chrono.
kkt-clock.must_not: Let a chrono type into its public surface.

kkt-names.concern: Avatars' handles, channel IDs, the name packs, and the randomness behind them (`Entropy`).

kkt-shutdown.concern: The stop signal (Ctrl-C, SIGTERM) and the `Shutdown` that ends the server.
kkt-shutdown.must_not: Let a tokio-util type out of the crate.

kkt-logs.concern: The log file the server writes itself, rolled over and pruned within its policy.

kkt-provenance.concern: What produced a server run: the build, its git commit, and the settings that shape the run.
kkt-provenance.must_not: Store the run record: kkt-server does.

kkt-scratch.concern: Tests' scratch folders under `target/tmp`, named for the test and removed when dropped.
